# ECN-2026-010 - Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Reason for change
- Background: During routine inspections and operational trend review for EQ-P3-L1-IH03, cooling system performance was identified as a recurring contributor to heater trips and premature coil wear. Field verification and hydraulic assessment indicated the coil cooling water flow threshold used in operational checks and interlock settings was below the level required to maintain stable coil temperature and to prevent accelerated insulation degradation. This change clarifies the minimum flow requirement that must be enforced in controls, SOPs, and maintenance checks.
- Rationale: Standardizing a documented minimum coil cooling water flow consolidates corrective actions already implemented in the field and eliminates ambiguity between operators, maintenance, and controls engineering. A clear minimum reduces variation in start-up and run procedures, decreases risk of thermal stress to the coil assembly, and supports longer coil life and more reliable production availability. This change is consistent with corrective recommendations referenced in ECN-2026-006 and aligns with normal operating expectations captured in SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02.

Affected items
- Equipment affected: EQ-P3-L1-IH03 (Hot Forge induction billet heater #3). All physical coils, their flow measurement and control subsystems, flow interlock logic, operator displays, and maintenance documentation for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 are within scope.
- Procedures affected: SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 require update to reference the clarified coil cooling water flow minimum and to align step wording and interlock verification steps with the new requirement.
- Control and instrumentation: Flow transmitter scaling, alarm thresholds, and interlock setpoints for coil cooling on EQ-P3-L1-IH03 must be updated to reflect the minimum flow requirement. Operator HMI text and alarm descriptions must be revised where they reference coil flow limits.
- Training and records: Operator and maintenance training materials specific to EQ-P3-L1-IH03 must be amended. Change training attendance and competency records must be retained in the maintenance document control folder for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.

Implementation
- New minimum flow requirement: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. This value will be used as the definitive minimum for control interlocks, alarm thresholds, operator checklists, and maintenance acceptance criteria for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.
- Control updates: Controls engineering will update flow transmitter scaling and interlock setpoints on the EQ-P3-L1-IH03 control system to reference 65 L/min. Alarm text will state the minimum explicitly and reference this ECN where interlock logic or manual override justification is required.
- Procedure updates: SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 will be revised to incorporate the coil cooling water flow minimum. The relevant procedure sections will be rephrased to instruct operators to verify that flow meets or exceeds the documented minimum before heater energization and to document flow readings in the shift log. Procedure update shall include guidance for actions when flow is below the minimum, consistent with safe shutdown and notification steps.
- Maintenance actions: Maintenance inspection checklists for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 will add a dedicated step to confirm measured flow against 65 L/min during post-repair commissioning and periodic verification tasks. Flow metering calibration checks will be scheduled and recorded following any instrumentation work.
- Training: A targeted briefing will be delivered to operations and maintenance teams responsible for EQ-P3-L1-IH03. Briefing will cover the reason for the change, how to interpret the flow reading, control behavior when flow is below the minimum, and documentation expectations. Attendance will be recorded and training materials attached to the equipment file.
- Examples and expected behavior: Example scenarios will be provided in the procedure updates. Example text will show an operator verifying coil cooling water flow on the local HMI and documenting the reading in the shift log prior to heater energization. Another example will describe steps to take when flow drops below the minimum during operation, including safe ramp down and notification of maintenance and engineering.
- Records to keep: The following records will be created and retained in the EQ-P3-L1-IH03 document folder: control change log documenting setpoint updates referencing this ECN, updated versions of SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02, flow verification checklist entries demonstrating compliance with 65 L/min during commissioning or after repairs, training attendance records for affected personnel, and a brief incident log for any events where flow fell below the minimum after implementation.

Approvals
- Engineering approval: Responsible process and controls engineers will sign to confirm control updates and procedural wording are complete and that the change achieves the intended operational objective for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.
- Operations approval: Operations management will confirm procedural updates and training satisfy operational readiness for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and that operator materials are aligned with plant practice.
- Maintenance approval: Maintenance leadership will confirm additions to maintenance checklists and recordkeeping practices for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.
- Document references: Implementers must consult ECN-2026-006 for preceding corrective details and follow procedural change control steps in SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 when updating and releasing revised procedures.

Change control note
- This ECN establishes the authoritative minimum coil cooling water flow for EQ-P3-L1-IH03. All stakeholders must reference this ECN when performing work, updating documentation, or assessing operational events related to coil cooling on Hot Forge induction billet heater #3.
